captions.instagram:
How does a pressure cooker work?

A 70-gram weight on a hole 3 mm across holds back steam pushing like 380 kg on the lid. Take an Indian whistle cooker apart in 3D, count its whistles, and see why 120 °C cooks dal four times faster.

→ A pressure cooker is a pot that seals: a lid, a rubber gasket, and a small weight on a thin pipe.
→ The weight sits on a hole 3 mm across. Steam must push 97,000 pascals to lift it.
→ That is about 2 atmospheres inside, so water stays liquid until about 120 °C.
→ When the pressure lifts the weight, steam rushes out and the cooker whistles.
→ The escaping steam carries heat away, the pressure drops, the weight falls back, and it starts again.

youtubeLong.title: How does a pressure cooker work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
A 70-gram weight on a hole 3 mm across holds back steam pushing like 380 kg on the lid. Take an Indian whistle cooker apart in 3D, count its whistles, and see why 120 °C cooks dal four times faster.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/pressurecookerclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/pressurecookerclear

In this video:
• A pot that seals. A pressure cooker is a strong pot whose lid seals with a rubber gasket.
• The weight sets the pressure. Steam can only escape by lifting the weight, so it lifts when pressure × the hole's area equals the weight's force.
• Why it whistles again and again. When the weight lifts, steam rushes out at about 2 g a second and carries heat away faster than the flame adds it.
• Hotter means much faster. Wet food cannot get hotter than the water's boiling point.
• Layers of safety. If froth blocks the vent, the pressure climbs until the fusible plug gives way, which India's standard IS 2347 says must happen before 3 kgf/cm².
• From Papin to the multicooker. Denis Papin showed a steam digester with a weighted safety valve in 1679.
